note: The quantisation sweep. Every variant here is built, run and reported; a variant that fails to build or fails to load is reported as a failure rather than dropped.

variants.name: fp32
variants.why: Baseline. Everything else is measured against this.

variants.name: int8-dynamic
variants.why: Weight-only INT8 with run-time activation ranges. No calibration data needed.

variants.name: int8-static
variants.why: The recommended recipe: calibrated INT8 with the decode tail left in float32.

variants.name: int8-static-c16
variants.why: Same recipe with an eighth of the calibration images, to show how much calibration set size matters.

variants.name: int8-static-pertensor
variants.why: One weight scale per tensor instead of per output channel.

variants.name: int8-static-entropy
variants.not_measured_reason: onnxruntime's entropy calibrator holds the collected activation tensors in memory and was killed by the OOM killer on the 3.7 GB machine these numbers were measured on, at both 128 and 16 calibration images. Set enabled to true to run it on a machine with more memory.

variants.name: int8-static-notail
variants.why: The naive recipe that quantises the whole graph including the decode tail. Included to show what it does.
